question.text: Satpura Market-Neutral Fund's distributor is offering potential investors a 'one-time discount of 0.5% on the subscription amount' if they invest in the fund by month-end. Under SEBI (PFUTP) Regulations, 2003, this practice is:

answer.text: Permitted as long as the discount is disclosed in the PPM
Prohibited as a 'pass-back', representing an unfair trade practice and conflict of interest
Permitted up to 1% of subscription amount

explanation.text: The Logic: Pass-backs — indirect incentives to investors to subscribe — are explicitly prohibited under SEBI (PFUTP) Regulations. They create a conflict because investors are discouraged from evaluating the fund on its investment merits. AIFs and their distributors must abstain from pass-backs regardless of category. The Trap: Options A, B, D introduce fictitious tolerances. PFUTP admits no such carve-outs. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/B (Distributors) and III-A (Compliance) test pass-backs. XIX-E tests from Manager-side compliance-oversight angle. Manager's Pro-Tip: Manager is on the hook even if distributor initiates the pass-back — document distributor code-of-conduct training, keep whistle-blower channel open. Also prohibited: soft-dollar arrangements, assured returns.
